# `silk/time/calendar_data`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Tables of the calendars of `silk.time.calendar` that cannot be computed with a short rule.

## When to use

Use `silk.time.calendar` and not this module. The tables are public only because the calendar
module reads them.

## Details

- [`CHINESE_YEARS`](#CHINESE_YEARS) and [`DANGI_YEARS`](#DANGI_YEARS) have one number for each year from 1800 to 2200. The
  year of the table is the ISO 8601 year in which the lunar year starts.
- [`UMALQURA_MONTHS`](#UMALQURA_MONTHS) and [`UMALQURA_STARTS`](#UMALQURA_STARTS) have the Umm al-Qura calendar of Saudi Arabia for
  the years 1300 to 1600 of the Hijra.
- [`PERSIAN_EARLY_YEARS`](#PERSIAN_EARLY_YEARS) has the years of the Persian calendar that start one day earlier
  than the 33-year rule says.

## Examples

### Read the first year of the Chinese table

```silk
import silk.time.calendar_data as CalendarData

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // Bits 6 to 9 have the number of the month that is repeated, or 0. In 1800 it is month 4.
  let leap = (CalendarData.CHINESE_YEARS[0] / 64) % 16
  if leap != 4 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `CalendarData` with `import silk.time.calendar_data as CalendarData`.

<a id="CHINESE_YEARS"></a>

## `CHINESE_YEARS`

```silk
pub const CHINESE_YEARS: [i32; 401]
```

The years of the Chinese calendar from 1800 to 2200, one number for each year.

### Details

Bit 0 is the ISO month of the new year minus 1, bits 1 to 5 are its day minus 1, bits 6 to 9
are the number of the month that is repeated or 0, and bit `10 + n` is 1 when month `n + 1` of
the year, counted from the new year, has 30 days and 0 when it has 29.

<a id="DANGI_YEARS"></a>

## `DANGI_YEARS`

```silk
pub const DANGI_YEARS: [i32; 401]
```

The years of the Korean Dangi calendar from 1800 to 2200, one number for each year.

### Details

Bit 0 is the ISO month of the new year minus 1, bits 1 to 5 are its day minus 1, bits 6 to 9
are the number of the month that is repeated or 0, and bit `10 + n` is 1 when month `n + 1` of
the year, counted from the new year, has 30 days and 0 when it has 29.

<a id="UMALQURA_MONTHS"></a>

## `UMALQURA_MONTHS`

```silk
pub const UMALQURA_MONTHS: [i32; 301]
```

The month lengths of the Umm al-Qura years 1300 to 1600: bit `12 - m` is 1 when month `m` has
30 days and 0 when it has 29.

## `UMALQURA_STARTS`

```silk
pub const UMALQURA_STARTS: [i32; 302]
```

The first day of the Umm al-Qura years 1300 to 1601, in days from the first day of year 1 of

<a id="PERSIAN_EARLY_YEARS"></a>

## `PERSIAN_EARLY_YEARS`

```silk
pub const PERSIAN_EARLY_YEARS: [i32; 78]
```

The years of the Persian calendar, in rising order, that start one day earlier than the
33-year rule says, because the year before them does not have the leap day that the rule gives.
